result_text:
Template literals are now masked the same way as the other string literals when units are compared, but I haven't tested the new behaviour. I did not add a test for the two-functions case or run it.

The change is an override of `extraCleanContent` in `JavaScriptHeuristicUnitsExtractor.java`. It collapses each `` `...` `` literal, including multi-line ones and any `${...}` inside, to ` `` ` before the existing normalization runs. Because the literal is gone before the slash masking runs, slashes inside it are no longer what hides the difference. Code outside the literals is untouched, so a difference there still keeps units apart.

I put it in the JavaScript extractor only, because the shared C-style one is used by Go, Kotlin and others, where backticks mean something else. TypeScript wasn't checked, and the override only applies if TypeScript uses this extractor.

I ran the existing `*JavaScript*` and `*Unit*` tests in `codeanalyzer`. The command printed no failures, but I didn't check the exit status.
